title: GATHER Activity 2 Measure Questions
subtitle: Five literature-grounded prompts for community refinement of future measurement domains.

projectContext.primaryQuestion: How do Native community members and Indigenous knowledge holders define the healing impacts of food sovereignty on substance use recovery, chronic pain management, mental wellbeing, and relational wellness?
projectContext.activity2Purpose: Use community and knowledge-holder guidance to develop domains, language, safeguards, and candidate indicators for a culturally grounded survey instrument.
measurementFilters: directly serves recovery, chronic pain, mental wellbeing, or relational wellness
adds something not already covered by the listening guide
addresses an under-tested or under-validated measurement gap
moves beyond participation frequency into meaning, access, relationship, and impact
centers strengths, healing, cultural continuity, responsibility, and thriving
fits an urban, intertribal context without assuming one practice or Nation
uses community language rather than technical scale language
respects knowledge that should stay protected, sacred, qualitative, or story-held
supports future community action, advocacy, program design, or institutional accountability
projectContext.scopeNote: These are optional probes for listening sessions and scholar interviews, not final survey items or technical scale language.

recommendations.title: Test embodied healing and balance.
recommendations.candidateMeasure: Whole-person healing support: pain, stress, cravings, grief, balance, grounding, and hard-day coping connected to food, plants, land, or cultural practice.
recommendations.move: Add a nonclinical embodied-healing question so recovery, pain management, and mental wellbeing do not disappear under broad wellness language.
recommendations.why: This candidate is promising for GATHER because it directly links food sovereignty to recovery, pain, and mental wellbeing. It still needs community interpretation because most existing measures come from clinical, stress-coping, or cultural-intervention literatures rather than a food-sovereignty-specific Indigenous measurement module.
recommendations.question: What signs would tell you that food, plants, land, shared meals, or cultural practice are helping someone get through pain, stress, cravings, grief, or a hard day, without asking them to share private details?
recommendations.listenFor: Signs of balance, grounding, routine, reduced isolation, spiritual support, emotional regulation, or practical support that could become future indicators without forcing disclosure.
recommendations.caution: Use only as an optional probe. Do not ask participants to disclose substance use, trauma, diagnosis, pain history, or medication details.
recommendations.keyCitations: S002 - Brown (2019); S020 - King, Smith, & Gracey (2009); S027 - Rowan et al. (2014); S031 - Walters, Simoni, & Evans-Campbell (2002)
recommendations.outcomeAlignment: Keeps recovery, pain, stress, cravings, grief, and balance visible without turning the session into clinical disclosure.

recommendations.title: Test cultural strengths and connectedness.
recommendations.candidateMeasure: Cultural strengths and connectedness: belonging, identity, language, values, humor, gratitude, spirituality, traditional foods, responsibility, and connection with relatives.
recommendations.move: Add a cultural-strengths question that lets participants affirm, reject, rename, or protect candidate domains surfaced in the measurement literature.
recommendations.why: The literature identifies cultural connectedness and values as protective, but measures are fragmented, inconsistently validated, and often developed outside the exact urban/intertribal GATHER context. Community language should determine what belongs in a future module.
recommendations.question: Some sources talk about cultural connection through belonging, identity, language, values, humor, gratitude, foods, spirituality, or responsibility to relatives. Which of those feel like signs of wellness here, which need different words, and which should stay in story or community guidance rather than a survey question?
recommendations.listenFor: Locally meaningful terms, strengths that are missing from existing tools, domains that should remain qualitative, and wording that avoids pan-Indigenous flattening.
recommendations.caution: Do not universalize one fixed list of cultural strengths or imply that cultural connection proves authenticity.
recommendations.keyCitations: S017 - Jacob et al. (2020); S021 - Walls et al. (2026); S031 - Walters, Simoni, & Evans-Campbell (2002)
recommendations.outcomeAlignment: Lets participants decide which cultural strengths are meaningful, locally worded, measurable, or better kept in story.

recommendations.title: Test food-land relationship and stewardship.
recommendations.candidateMeasure: Food-land relationship and cultural stewardship: reciprocal care, responsibility, intergenerational knowledge transmission, land/water/plant relationships, and community decision-making.
recommendations.move: Add a question that tests whether food sovereignty should be measured as relationship and responsibility, not only participation, diet, or food access.
recommendations.why: This is central to GATHER and IHEI's Food & Land Sovereignty work. The literature strongly supports it conceptually, but local participants should decide which relationships are meaningful, measurable, protected, or better held through story.
recommendations.question: When food sovereignty is happening in a good way, what relationships or responsibilities show it: with foods, plants, land, water, family, community, ancestors, future generations, or decision-making? What would this way of asking miss?
recommendations.listenFor: How participants distinguish food security from food sovereignty, whether stewardship is individual or collective, and what should not be reduced to a score.
recommendations.caution: Do not ask for sacred, ceremonial, ecological-location, or protected knowledge. Keep the urban/intertribal context open.
recommendations.keyCitations: S005 - Cote (2016); S016 - Hoover (2017); S018 - Jernigan et al. (2023); S022 - Morrison (2011); S028 - Sowerwine et al. (2023)
recommendations.outcomeAlignment: Keeps food sovereignty distinct from food security by asking about relationship, reciprocal care, and responsibility.

recommendations.title: Test access and enabling conditions.
recommendations.candidateMeasure: Access and enabling conditions: land access, cost, time, disability, transportation, tools, permissions, knowledge transmission, policy, safety, and institutional support.
recommendations.move: Add a structural access question so future indicators do not mistake barriers for lack of interest, cultural value, or personal choice.
recommendations.why: This candidate serves applied GATHER goals because it can guide advocacy, program support, and institutional readiness. It needs community input because access barriers vary by place, generation, health, disability, displacement, and relationship to Native community.
recommendations.question: What makes it easier or harder for people to be in relationship with traditional foods, plants, land, or stewardship practices, and how should future questions avoid mistaking barriers for lack of interest or connection?
recommendations.listenFor: Concrete supports, structural barriers, accessibility needs, urban/intertribal realities, and ways to word future survey items without deficit framing.
recommendations.caution: Keep this strengths-based and structural. Do not turn barriers into a deficit story about participants or community.
recommendations.keyCitations: S008 - Ecotrust (2023); S009 - Ecotrust (2024); S010 - Ecotrust (2025); S019 - Jernigan et al. (2017); S026 - Reading & Wien (2009)
recommendations.outcomeAlignment: Prevents future indicators from mistaking structural barriers for lack of interest, connection, or personal choice.

recommendations.title: Test measurement governance and benefit.
recommendations.candidateMeasure: Measurement governance and collective benefit: who defines meaning, who controls data, what stays protected, how interpretation happens, and how information benefits community.
recommendations.move: Add a future-measurement governance question before candidate indicators move into a survey module.
recommendations.why: OCAP, CARE, Indigenous data sovereignty, and IHEI's health/data justice frame all make governance part of measurement validity. A measure is not useful if it extracts knowledge, invites misinterpretation, or fails to support community benefit and self-determination.
recommendations.question: If these stories later become survey questions or indicators, who should decide what the answers mean, what should be protected or kept in story, and how should the information benefit community?
recommendations.listenFor: Rules for ownership, control, access, interpretation, dissemination, Council/community review, protected knowledge, and concrete community benefit.
recommendations.caution: Ask as refinement, not approval. Community authority over meaning, interpretation, use, and benefit should be explicit.
recommendations.keyCitations: S004 - Carroll et al. (2020); S011 - FNIGC (n.d.); S012 - FNIGC (2022); S021 - Walls et al. (2026); S030 - Walter & Suina (2019)
recommendations.outcomeAlignment: Makes governance, interpretation, protection, and community benefit part of measurement validity from the start.

safeguards: Do not add a long measurement module to the listening session.
Do not ask for sacred, ceremonial, ecological-location, or protected knowledge.
Do not treat food insecurity, diet, or participation frequency as food sovereignty by itself.
Do not ask participants to disclose trauma, substance use, diagnosis, pain history, or medication details.
Do not combine cultural identity, belonging, spirituality, language, foods, land relationship, and governance into one broad culture score.
